topics.name: Introduction to Java
topics.summary: Trace a program from Java source to a running JVM.

subTopics.name: History of Java
subTopics.summary: Follow Oak from a device project to Java's public launch and key releases.

subTopics.name: Features of Java (Platform Independent, OOP, etc.)
subTopics.summary: Connect portability, object-oriented design, and managed memory to real programs.

subTopics.name: JDK, JRE, JVM Architecture
subTopics.summary: Separate the tools in the JDK, the runtime libraries, and the JVM that executes bytecode.

subTopics.name: Compilation and Execution Process
subTopics.summary: Follow javac output through class loading, linking, initialization, and execution.

subTopics.name: Bytecode and Platform Independence
subTopics.summary: Read a class file with javap and explain why compatible JVMs can share it.

subTopics.name: Java Editions (SE, EE, ME)
subTopics.summary: Pick Java SE for general use, Jakarta EE for enterprise APIs, or Java ME for supported devices.

subTopics.name: Path and Classpath (Environment Variables)
subTopics.summary: Check PATH when a command is missing and the classpath when Java needs a class or JAR.

subTopics.name: First Java Program structure and main method
subTopics.summary: Run Hello World, pass a command-line argument, and trace how it reaches main.

subTopics.name: Java Keywords and Identifiers
subTopics.summary: Spot reserved words and choose clear, valid names for variables and types.

subTopics.name: Comments in Java (Single-line, Multi-line, Documentation)
subTopics.summary: Use line comments for short notes, block comments for longer notes, and Javadoc for API docs.

subTopics.name: Java vs C++ comparison
subTopics.summary: Compare managed memory and JVM bytecode with C++ ownership and native builds.

subTopics.name: Java is Pass-by-Value
subTopics.summary: Java copies every argument value, including references. Mutating an object differs from assigning a new reference.

topics.name: Data Types & Variables
topics.summary: Choose a type, convert it safely, and put each variable in the right scope.

subTopics.name: Primitive data types
subTopics.summary: Pick from eight primitive types for numbers, characters, and booleans.

subTopics.name: Reference types
subTopics.summary: A reference points to an object or is null. Assigning it does not copy the object.

subTopics.name: Type casting and conversion
subTopics.summary: Widening often happens automatically. Narrowing needs a cast and can lose information.

subTopics.name: Variables (local, instance, static)
subTopics.summary: Use local variables for temporary work, instance fields per object, and static fields per class.

topics.name: Operators & Control Statements
topics.summary: Write a condition, repeat work, and leave a block at the right time.

subTopics.name: Arithmetic, Logical, Relational operators
subTopics.summary: Calculate values, compare them, and use short-circuit boolean operators to skip unnecessary work.

subTopics.name: If-else, switch statements
subTopics.summary: Use if for flexible conditions and switch for choices based on one value or pattern.

subTopics.name: Loops (for, while, do-while, enhanced for)
subTopics.summary: Pick a for loop for counted work, a while loop for conditions, or enhanced for for iteration.

subTopics.name: Break, continue, return statements
subTopics.summary: Break leaves a loop, continue skips to the next iteration, and return exits the method.

topics.name: Arrays & Basic I/O
topics.summary: Collect values in arrays and read simple input from the console.

subTopics.name: Single and multidimensional arrays
subTopics.summary: An array has fixed length. A multidimensional Java array contains references to other arrays.

subTopics.name: Array manipulation
subTopics.summary: Use indexing, copying, and sorting to transform a fixed-size array.

subTopics.name: Jagged arrays
subTopics.summary: Give each row its own length when the data is uneven.

subTopics.name: Scanner class and Console I/O
subTopics.summary: Use Scanner for tokenized input. A system console may be unavailable in an IDE.

topics.name: Classes and Objects
topics.summary: Create objects and predict what runs when they are initialized.

subTopics.name: Class definition and object creation
subTopics.summary: A class defines fields and methods. Each new instance can hold its own state.

subTopics.name: Constructors (default, parameterized, copy)
subTopics.summary: Use constructors to build valid objects. Java supplies a default constructor only when none is declared.

subTopics.name: Constructor overloading
subTopics.summary: Offer different parameter lists and delegate shared initialization with this(...).

subTopics.name: this keyword
subTopics.summary: Use this for the current instance, to distinguish fields, or to call another constructor.

subTopics.name: Object Initialization Order
subTopics.summary: Superclass initialization precedes subclass instance initializers and constructor bodies.

topics.name: Encapsulation
topics.summary: Protect an object's rules with a small, intentional public API.

subTopics.name: Access modifiers (private, public, protected, default)
subTopics.summary: Choose private, package access, protected, or public based on who needs the member.

subTopics.name: Getters and Setters
subTopics.summary: Expose only the changes callers need and validate them before updating state.

subTopics.name: Data hiding
subTopics.summary: Keep internal fields private and control how callers read or change them.

topics.name: Inheritance & Composition
topics.summary: Know when to extend a type and when to give it a collaborator.

subTopics.name: Types of inheritance
subTopics.summary: A Java class can extend one class and implement multiple interfaces.

subTopics.name: super keyword
subTopics.summary: Use super to call a superclass constructor or access an inherited implementation.

subTopics.name: Method overriding
subTopics.summary: Replace inherited instance behavior with a compatible method and let the runtime pick it.

subTopics.name: final keyword
subTopics.summary: A final variable cannot be reassigned, a final method cannot be overridden, and a final class cannot be extended.

subTopics.name: IS-A vs HAS-A relationship
subTopics.summary: Use inheritance for a genuine subtype and composition when an object uses another object.

topics.name: Polymorphism
topics.summary: Distinguish selecting a method signature from selecting its implementation.

subTopics.name: Compile-time (Method Overloading)
subTopics.summary: The compiler chooses among same-name methods using the argument types and applicable conversions.

subTopics.name: Runtime (Method Overriding)
subTopics.summary: A subclass can override an inherited instance method to supply its own behavior.

subTopics.name: Dynamic method dispatch
subTopics.summary: Java dispatches an overridden instance method based on the actual object's type.

topics.name: Abstraction
topics.summary: Describe what callers can rely on while keeping implementation details flexible.

subTopics.name: Abstract classes and methods
subTopics.summary: Share a base implementation and require subclasses to fill in abstract methods.

subTopics.name: Interfaces
subTopics.summary: Define a contract that different classes can implement.

subTopics.name: Multiple inheritance using interfaces
subTopics.summary: A class can implement multiple interfaces and may need to resolve conflicting default methods.

subTopics.name: Marker interfaces
subTopics.summary: A marker interface, such as Serializable, signals a property without declaring methods.

topics.name: Static keyword
topics.summary: Recognize members that belong to a class and when they initialize.

subTopics.name: Static variables and methods
subTopics.summary: Static fields are shared by instances of the class. Static methods have no this reference.

subTopics.name: Static blocks
subTopics.summary: A static block runs during initialization of its class.

subTopics.name: Static nested classes
subTopics.summary: A static nested class can be used without an instance of the enclosing class.

topics.name: Inner Classes
topics.summary: Choose a nested type based on scope and access to the enclosing instance.

subTopics.name: Member inner class
subTopics.summary: A non-static member class carries a reference to an enclosing instance.

subTopics.name: Static nested class
subTopics.summary: A static nested class has no implicit enclosing instance.

subTopics.name: Local inner class
subTopics.summary: A local class lives inside a block and can capture effectively final local variables.

subTopics.name: Anonymous inner class
subTopics.summary: An anonymous class defines and instantiates an implementation at the same time.

topics.name: Packages
topics.summary: Group related types and control what other packages can see.

subTopics.name: Creating and using packages
subTopics.summary: Declare a package to group types under a qualified name.

subTopics.name: Import statements
subTopics.summary: An import lets you refer to another type by its simple name.

subTopics.name: Access protection
subTopics.summary: Package access limits a member to its package. Protected also supports subclass access under specific rules.

topics.name: Object Class Methods
topics.summary: Make custom objects work predictably with collections, logging, and copying.

subTopics.name: equals() and hashCode() contract
subTopics.summary: Equal objects must have equal hash codes. Keep equality fields stable while objects are hash keys.

subTopics.name: toString()
subTopics.summary: Supply a readable representation useful for debugging and avoid printing secrets.

subTopics.name: clone()
subTopics.summary: Object.clone makes a shallow copy. A copy constructor can make ownership choices explicit.

subTopics.name: finalize()
subTopics.summary: Finalization is deprecated for removal and is unreliable for cleanup. Use try-with-resources instead.

topics.name: Core Exception Handling
topics.summary: Trace failures, catch only what you can handle, and close resources reliably.

subTopics.name: Fundamentals
subTopics.summary: Follow a Throwable from the point it is thrown to a matching handler or thread exit.

subTopics.name: Exception Hierarchy
subTopics.summary: Distinguish Error, checked exceptions, and RuntimeException using the Throwable hierarchy.

subTopics.name: Checked vs Unchecked Exceptions
subTopics.summary: The compiler requires checked exceptions to be caught or declared. Runtime exceptions and errors are unchecked.

subTopics.name: try–catch–finally blocks
subTopics.summary: Catch a recoverable type and use finally when cleanup must run after either outcome.

subTopics.name: Multi-Catch and try-with-resources
subTopics.summary: Group compatible exception types in one catch and close resources automatically with try-with-resources.

subTopics.name: throw vs throws keyword
subTopics.summary: Throw raises an exception object. A throws clause declares possible exceptions in a method signature.

subTopics.name: Custom Exceptions
subTopics.summary: Create a specific exception when callers benefit from recognizing a distinct failure.

subTopics.name: Exception Propagation
subTopics.summary: An uncaught exception moves through callers until a matching handler is found.

subTopics.name: Exception Chaining
subTopics.summary: When translating an exception, attach the original as its cause.

subTopics.name: Best Practices for Core Java Exception Handling
subTopics.summary: Handle at the layer that can recover, preserve causes, and keep catch blocks specific.

topics.name: Collection Interfaces
topics.summary: Pick the collection contract that matches your data and access pattern.

subTopics.name: Collection, List, Set, Queue, Map
subTopics.summary: Lists keep position, sets enforce uniqueness, queues schedule removal, and maps associate keys with values.

subTopics.name: Iterator, ListIterator, and Spliterator
subTopics.summary: Use Iterator to traverse, ListIterator to move both ways, and Spliterator to partition traversal.

topics.name: Implementations
topics.summary: Compare collection implementations by order, access cost, and concurrency behavior.

subTopics.name: ArrayList, LinkedList, Vector, Stack
subTopics.summary: Use ArrayList for indexed access and prefer a Deque to legacy Stack for stack operations.

subTopics.name: HashSet, LinkedHashSet, TreeSet
subTopics.summary: Choose HashSet for membership, LinkedHashSet for encounter order, or TreeSet for sorted elements.

subTopics.name: HashMap, LinkedHashMap, TreeMap
subTopics.summary: Choose HashMap for lookup, LinkedHashMap for encounter order, and TreeMap for sorted keys.

subTopics.name: Hashtable and ConcurrentHashMap
subTopics.summary: Prefer ConcurrentHashMap for concurrent access and note that it rejects null keys and values.

subTopics.name: PriorityQueue and ArrayDeque
subTopics.summary: Use PriorityQueue when priority sets the order and ArrayDeque for a stack or FIFO queue.

topics.name: Sorting and Utility
topics.summary: Sort data with an intentional order and reuse Java's collection utilities.

subTopics.name: Comparable vs Comparator
subTopics.summary: Comparable defines natural order. Comparator supplies a separate ordering for a particular task.

subTopics.name: Collections and Arrays utility classes
subTopics.summary: Use Arrays for arrays and Collections helpers for collection operations such as sorting and searching.

topics.name: Generic Classes and Methods
topics.summary: Parameterize a class or method to reuse it while keeping compile-time type checks.

topics.name: Bounded Type Parameters
topics.summary: Use a bound such as T extends Number to state which types are accepted and which operations are available.

topics.name: Wildcards (?, extends, super)
topics.summary: Accept related generic types with ? extends for reading and ? super for writing.

topics.name: PECS Principle
topics.summary: Read PECS as producer extends, consumer super, then use it to design a type-safe copy method.

topics.name: Type Erasure
topics.summary: Generic type arguments are mostly erased at runtime. Explain why List<String> and List<Integer> have the same runtime class.

topics.name: Thread Basics
topics.summary: Create a task and understand what can pause, finish, or interrupt its thread.

subTopics.name: Thread class vs Runnable interface
subTopics.summary: Runnable describes the work. A Thread is one way to execute it.

subTopics.name: Thread lifecycle
subTopics.summary: Track a thread from creation through runnable, waiting, or blocked states to termination.

subTopics.name: sleep, join, yield, interrupt
subTopics.summary: Sleep pauses, join waits for another thread, yield is a hint, and interrupt requests cooperation.

topics.name: Synchronization
topics.summary: Protect shared state and recognize when threads stop making progress.

subTopics.name: synchronized keyword (blocks/methods)
subTopics.summary: A synchronized block or method takes a monitor and coordinates visibility as well as exclusive access.

subTopics.name: Locking: Object level vs Class level
subTopics.summary: An instance monitor protects one object. A static synchronized method takes the Class object's monitor.

subTopics.name: volatile keyword
subTopics.summary: Volatile gives visibility for a field but does not make a compound operation such as increment atomic.

subTopics.name: Deadlock, Livelock, and Starvation
subTopics.summary: Deadlock blocks progress, livelock keeps reacting without progress, and starvation denies a thread its turn.

topics.name: Inter-thread Communication
topics.summary: Coordinate waiting and notification around the condition that actually matters.

subTopics.name: wait, notify, and notifyAll
subTopics.summary: Call wait and notification methods while holding the monitor. Recheck the condition after waking.

subTopics.name: Producer-Consumer problem
subTopics.summary: Use a BlockingQueue when producers and consumers need safe handoff or bounded capacity.

topics.name: Concurrency Utilities
topics.summary: Choose an executor, a result type, or a coordination tool that fits the job.

subTopics.name: Executor Framework and Thread Pools
subTopics.summary: Executors separate task submission from thread management. Choose capacity and shut them down deliberately.

subTopics.name: Callable and Future
subTopics.summary: Callable returns a result or throws. Future represents the pending result and can be cancelled.

subTopics.name: CompletableFuture
subTopics.summary: Chain asynchronous stages and decide how failures and execution scheduling should be handled.

subTopics.name: Locks (ReentrantLock, ReadWriteLock)
subTopics.summary: ReentrantLock supports explicit locking strategies. ReadWriteLock separates shared reads from exclusive writes.

subTopics.name: Atomic variables
subTopics.summary: Atomic types give atomic operations on individual variables, such as compare-and-set.

subTopics.name: CountDownLatch and CyclicBarrier
subTopics.summary: A latch opens after a countdown. A barrier lets a group wait for one another at a common point.

topics.name: Java 8 Features
topics.summary: Use Java 8's functional tools to transform data, express absence, and work with time.

subTopics.name: Lambda Expressions
subTopics.summary: A lambda supplies behavior for a functional interface without an anonymous class body.

subTopics.name: Functional Interfaces
subTopics.summary: A functional interface has one abstract method and can be a target for a lambda.

subTopics.name: Stream API
subTopics.summary: Build a pipeline with intermediate operations and execute it with a terminal operation.

subTopics.name: Optional Class
subTopics.summary: Use Optional to represent a result that may be absent and handle that case explicitly.

subTopics.name: Default and Static methods in Interfaces
subTopics.summary: Default methods supply inherited behavior. Static interface methods belong to the interface itself.

subTopics.name: Date and Time API (java.time)
subTopics.summary: Use java.time types such as Instant, LocalDate, and ZonedDateTime for distinct time concepts.

topics.name: Java 9 to 11 Features
topics.summary: Compare the modularity, tooling, and library changes introduced from Java 9 through 11.

subTopics.name: Module System (JPMS)
subTopics.summary: A module declares dependencies and which packages it exports or opens.

subTopics.name: Private methods in Interfaces
subTopics.summary: Private interface methods let default methods share implementation details without exposing them.

subTopics.name: JShell
subTopics.summary: Use JShell to try small expressions or snippets before writing a full program.

subTopics.name: var keyword (Local Variable Type Inference)
subTopics.summary: Var asks the compiler to infer an initialized local variable's static type.

subTopics.name: HTTP Client API
subTopics.summary: Use Java 11's HttpClient for synchronous or asynchronous HTTP requests.

topics.name: Java 12 to 17 Features (Java 17 LTS)
topics.summary: Use newer syntax to make data, branches, and allowed subtypes easier to read.

subTopics.name: Switch Expressions
subTopics.summary: Return a value from switch and use arrow cases to avoid accidental fall-through.

subTopics.name: Text Blocks
subTopics.summary: Write multiline strings with text blocks and check how indentation is handled.

subTopics.name: Records
subTopics.summary: Use records for transparent data carriers with generated accessors and value methods.

subTopics.name: Sealed Classes
subTopics.summary: Restrict which types can directly extend or implement the sealed type.

subTopics.name: Pattern Matching for instanceof
subTopics.summary: Bind a variable as part of an instanceof check to avoid a separate cast.

topics.name: Java 21 Features (LTS)
topics.summary: Explore virtual threads and the collection and pattern tools finalized in Java 21.

subTopics.name: Virtual Threads (Project Loom)
subTopics.summary: Run many blocking tasks with virtual threads while still limiting scarce resources such as database connections.

subTopics.name: Sequenced Collections
subTopics.summary: Sequenced interfaces expose first and last elements and a reversed view for ordered collections.

subTopics.name: Record Patterns
subTopics.summary: Destructure record components directly in a pattern.

subTopics.name: Pattern Matching for Switch
subTopics.summary: Match types in a switch and use exhaustiveness checking where applicable.

topics.name: String immutability and String Pool
topics.summary: Strings are immutable. The pool can share equal literals, while equals compares character values.

topics.name: String vs StringBuilder vs StringBuffer
topics.summary: Keep String for fixed text, StringBuilder for repeated edits, and StringBuffer when its synchronized operations fit.

topics.name: Common String methods
topics.summary: Use methods such as equals, indexOf, substring, and strip to compare or transform text.

topics.name: String formatting and manipulation
topics.summary: Format values with an explicit locale when needed and use builders for repeated assembly.

topics.name: Pattern and Matcher classes
topics.summary: Compile reusable regex patterns and use a Matcher to find matches or test the whole input.

topics.name: Regex metacharacters and quantifiers
topics.summary: Read anchors, character classes, and quantifiers before making a pattern more complex.

topics.name: Groups and capturing
topics.summary: Capture parts of a match for extraction and use non-capturing groups when only grouping is needed.

topics.name: Common regex patterns for validation
topics.summary: Use a small pattern for format checks and use explicit parsing for rules a regex cannot verify.

topics.name: Byte Streams vs Character Streams
topics.summary: Use byte streams for raw data and readers or writers for text with an explicit charset.

topics.name: BufferedReader and BufferedWriter
topics.summary: Buffer text operations, read lines when appropriate, and close or flush resources as needed.

topics.name: Java NIO (Path, Files, Channels)
topics.summary: Represent paths with Path, perform common file operations with Files, and use channels for lower-level I/O.

topics.name: Serialization and Deserialization (transient, serialVersionUID)
topics.summary: Understand how object graphs are serialized, what transient excludes by default, and how serialVersionUID affects compatibility.

topics.name: Externalizable interface
topics.summary: Implement Externalizable when the class must control its representation and reconstruction contract.

topics.name: Socket Programming (TCP/UDP)
topics.summary: Choose TCP for an ordered byte stream or UDP for independent datagrams and handle their different guarantees.

topics.name: URL and URLConnection
topics.summary: Use URL to represent a resource address and URLConnection for access through supported protocols.

topics.name: HttpURLConnection
topics.summary: Recognize the older HTTP API and compare its connection handling with Java's newer HttpClient.

topics.name: InetAddress class
topics.summary: Resolve host names and inspect IP addresses using InetAddress.

topics.name: JDBC Architecture and Drivers
topics.summary: Trace the JDBC call from application code through the driver to the database.

topics.name: Statement vs PreparedStatement vs CallableStatement
topics.summary: Use a plain Statement for fixed SQL, PreparedStatement for bound inputs, and CallableStatement for stored procedures.

topics.name: ResultSet and Transaction Management
topics.summary: Read query rows through ResultSet and group database writes with commit or rollback.

topics.name: Connection Pooling concepts
topics.summary: Reuse connections through a pool and size it against measured database capacity.

topics.name: JVM Architecture: ClassLoader, Runtime Data Areas, Execution Engine
topics.summary: Trace class loading, runtime memory, and bytecode execution as separate JVM responsibilities.

topics.name: Heap vs Stack Memory
topics.summary: Compare shared heap objects with the call frames held on each thread's stack.

topics.name: Garbage Collection Algorithms (G1, ZGC, etc.)
topics.summary: Compare collectors by pause time, throughput, and memory footprint on your workload.

topics.name: JIT Compiler and Memory Leaks
topics.summary: Distinguish JIT optimization from memory retention, then profile the problem you actually observe.

topics.name: Memory Model and happens-before relationship
topics.summary: Use happens-before relationships to reason about whether one thread can reliably see another's writes.

topics.name: Reference Types (Strong, Weak, Soft, Phantom)
topics.summary: Compare how strong, soft, weak, and phantom references affect reachability and cleanup.

topics.name: Cloning (Shallow vs Deep)
topics.summary: A shallow copy shares referenced objects. A deep copy duplicates the mutable state that needs isolation.

topics.name: Immutable Objects creation
topics.summary: Construct immutable objects by validating inputs and preventing mutable internals from escaping.

topics.name: Java Native Interface (JNI)
topics.summary: Use JNI to call native code and account for platform builds, memory ownership, and failure handling.

topics.name: Java Beans
topics.summary: Learn the JavaBeans conventions for properties and introspection. The name predates Spring beans.

topics.name: RMI (Remote Method Invocation)
topics.summary: Understand how RMI calls methods on remote Java objects and where local-call assumptions break down.

topics.name: Java Security Manager (Legacy, Disabled Since JDK 24)
topics.summary: Recognize the Security Manager in legacy code. It has been permanently disabled since JDK 24.

topics.name: Reflection API
topics.summary: Inspect classes or invoke members at runtime while respecting access and module boundaries.

topics.name: Annotations (Built-in and Custom)
topics.summary: Attach metadata with built-in or custom annotations and choose retention and targets deliberately.

topics.name: Enums
topics.summary: Use enums for a fixed set of named values that can carry behavior as well as data.

topics.name: Wrapper Classes and Autoboxing/Unboxing
topics.summary: Box primitives into wrapper objects and watch for null unboxing and identity comparisons.

topics.name: Internationalization (i18n) and Localization
topics.summary: Use resource bundles and locale-aware formats for text, dates, and numbers.

topics.name: JavaDoc and Code Documentation
topics.summary: Write Javadoc around caller expectations, accepted inputs, and meaningful failure behavior.

topics.name: SOLID Principles
topics.summary: Use SOLID to discuss responsibilities, extensibility, substitutability, interfaces, and dependency direction.

topics.name: Creational Design Patterns (Singleton, Factory, Builder)
topics.summary: Choose a Factory for creation decisions, a Builder for configurable construction, or a Singleton only for deliberate sharing.

topics.name: Structural Design Patterns (Adapter, Proxy, Decorator)
topics.summary: Adapt an interface, wrap an object with behavior, or control access through a proxy.

topics.name: Behavioral Design Patterns (Observer, Strategy)
topics.summary: Use Observer for notification and Strategy for interchangeable behavior.

topics.name: Clean Code principles
topics.summary: Prefer names and methods that say what the code does and make behavior easy to follow.

topics.name: Code smells and refactoring
topics.summary: Spot duplication or misplaced responsibilities and refactor in testable steps.

topics.name: Exception handling best practices
topics.summary: Catch failures where they can be handled, preserve useful causes, and close resources automatically.

topics.name: Naming conventions and coding standards
topics.summary: Apply established names and formatting consistently so reviewers can focus on behavior.

topics.name: Performance optimization techniques
topics.summary: Measure a representative workload, identify the bottleneck, and verify the change against the same workload.

topics.name: Unit Testing with JUnit and Mockito
topics.summary: Use JUnit for assertions and Mockito for test doubles when a real collaborator would obscure the behavior under test.
